question: Can eval and optimization data for a Foundry hosted agent live in native Foundry Datasets instead of inline, and exactly how?
mode: read-only: SDK source inspection, retained records, datasets.list/list_versions/get, official docs. No Azure write, no get_credentials/pending_upload (both mint SAS or may reserve).

a_datasets_api.answer: Native surface: project.datasets.{upload_file, upload_folder, pending_upload, create_or_update, get, list, list_versions, get_credentials, delete}. Registered version id form: azureai://accounts/<account>/projects/<project>/data/<name>/versions/<version>.
details: upload_file(name, version, file_path, connection_name=None, **upload_blob_kwargs) = pending_upload(BlobReference) -> ContainerClient.upload_blob(blob_name=file basename) -> create_or_update(FileDatasetVersion(data_uri=<blob url, query stripped>)). Returns FileDatasetVersion. No readback, no sha check, no stage recovery.

DatasetVersion fields: id (read), name, version, type uri_file|uri_folder, data_uri (dataUri), is_reference (read), connection_name, description, tags. Live list also returns displayName, isSingleFile, lifecycle, source, systemData.
get(name, version) on a missing version raises ResourceNotFoundError (UserError 'Could not find asset with ID: azureai://...').

b_eval_run_dataset_reference.answer: YES. Eval run data source `azure_ai_target_completions` accepts source {"type":"file_id","id":"<dataset version id azureai://...>"}; proven by a completed live run.
b_eval_run_dataset_reference.file_format: JSONL; each line is the bare item object (e.g. {"query": "..."}), NOT wrapped in {"item": ...} as file_content requires. Eval definition still needs a custom item_schema matching those fields.
evidence: testbeds/foundry-agent-evaluation/deploy/experiment.py:92 (dataset bytes = json.dumps({"query": q}) + newline per row)
b_eval_run_dataset_reference.not_proven: Name/version form (not azureai:// id) in file_id; folder datasets; row count > 3.

c_optimization_job_dataset_reference.answer: YES by SDK model and official quickstart; NOT yet proven live here. train_dataset and validation_dataset are discriminated AgentOptimizationDatasetInput: inline | reference.
c_optimization_job_dataset_reference.row_format: JSONL per official doc: {query (required), ground_truth?, criteria?[{name,instruction}]}; doc samples also carry an extra `name` field. SDK inline item model: query, ground_truth, desired_num_turns (1-20), criteria.
evidence: ~/.local/lib/python3.12/site-packages/azure/ai/projects/models/_models.py:2878-2915 (AgentOptimizationReferenceDatasetInput: type=reference, name required, version optional -> latest)

https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/agents/quickstarts/quickstart-optimize-hosted-agent (SDK path: train_dataset=AgentOptimizationReferenceDatasetInput(name, version); prerequisite 'A registered training dataset')
https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/agents/how-to/create-optimizer-dataset (Foundry dataset referenced by name+version; JSONL row fields)
https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/agents/concepts/agent-optimizer-overview ('Hosted-agent optimization supports local JSONL datasets and datasets registered in your Foundry project')
libraries/foundry-ops/src/foundry_ops/optimization/optimize.py:35-71 (current optimization_job hardwires inline_dataset for both splits)
c_optimization_job_dataset_reference.not_proven: Live job with reference train+validation; whether extra JSONL fields (id, case, expected_tools, split, zone...) are tolerated or rejected; whether version omission resolves to latest as documented.

d_limits.answer: No row or byte limit for inline items or datasets is documented in SDK docstrings. Only related bounds: desired_num_turns 1-20; code zip 250 MB (unrelated). foundry_ops MAX_INLINE_ITEMS=1000 and inline_dataset max_items=1000 are local bounds of unknown origin.
d_limits.confidence: medium (absence in docstrings grep; service limits unknown)
details: Docs: for a referenced dataset the service resolves row count before a cost estimate and refuses to estimate from an empty/unresolvable count.
Docs: every full evaluation invokes the agent once per row (baseline + each candidate), so cost scales with rows, not with inline-vs-reference.

result.testbed_dataset: GONE: get -> ResourceNotFoundError; list_versions -> 0 for both hosted-nonce-learning and migration-e-final-h-v3. Retired by the 2026-09-23 teardown (deploy/remediation-evidence/20260923-cleanup/teardown_manifest.py:376 calls project.datasets.delete; hosted-nonce-learning named in 20260923T082631464418Z-summary.json).

findings.fact: Inline data is already persisted by the service as native datasets with service-chosen names and version '1': optimization -> opt-inline-<job>[-val]; eval file_content -> eval-data-<timestamp>_UTC (assumes). Inline does not avoid dataset storage; it only loses caller-controlled name, version and sha pin.
Eval file_id with a dataset azureai:// version id is proven live (completed 3-row run).
Optimization reference input {type:reference,name,version} is the documented SDK path for hosted agents; not yet exercised in this repo.

E2E JSONL rows carry non-optimizer fields (case, expected_tools, express, id, split, weight_grams, zone). lifecycle.py projects them to ITEM_FIELDS before inline submission (template_apps/foundry_hosted_agent/deploy/lifecycle.py:888-890). A referenced dataset bypasses that projection, so the uploaded bytes must be the projected rows.
Testbed datasets were deleted in teardown; no registered caller-owned dataset currently exists in han-primary-foundry among the first 50 listed.

traps: Dataset version max 50 chars at create_or_update even though pending_upload accepts longer (71 observed); use sha256-<32 hex>, keep full sha as content pin (evals.py:20,38; .github/skills/foundry-native-agents/SKILL.md:108).

Managed storage lives in a provider subscription (d4b89623-..., RG hobov3_*), not the project subscription; containment checks must accept the project endpoint as origin (testbeds/foundry-agent-evaluation/deploy/records/dataset.json; SKILL.md:119).
SAS from pending_upload/get_credentials exists only in memory; never retain it. get_credentials is a POST that mints SAS: treat as credential-bearing, not a passive read.

pending_upload may retrieve or create a reservation; the testbed accumulated 4 reservations and one orphan blob. Record intent before each stage; never blind-retry (testbeds/foundry-agent-evaluation/deploy/records/20260922T074029199833Z-closeout.json next_decision).
upload_file does all three stages without readback or intent capture; SKILL.md:64 prefers staged native calls.
Eval file_id JSONL rows are bare items; file_content wraps each as {item: row}. Do not upload the wrapped form.
Optimization reference: version omitted = latest (mutable pointer). Always pin version.
Auto-created opt-inline-*/eval-data-* datasets and their blobs accumulate per run; teardown manifests must enumerate them (46+ eval-data present now).
SDK wire key is `items` for inline; `dataset_items` is the Python attribute only (optimize.py:3, SKILL.md:118).

proposed_foundry_ops_api.placement: New module foundry_ops/evaluation/datasets.py (or core/datasets.py if optimization must not depend on evaluation). assumes: optimization already imports from core only; choose core/ to keep dependency direction.

functions.behavior: Deterministic bytes: one json.dumps(row_projected, sort_keys=True, separators) + '\n' per row; refuses unknown/missing query. Reuses lifecycle _project rule; one owner.

functions.signature: register_jsonl_dataset(project, ledger, *, name: str, data: bytes, version: str | None = None) -> {id, name, version, sha256, bytes, data_uri, storage_account_arm_id, reused: bool}
functions.behavior: get -> reuse if present (then readback); else intent -> pending_upload(BlobReference) -> containment check -> upload_blob(overwrite=False) -> intent -> create_or_update(FileDatasetVersion) -> get -> readback. Lift from testbeds/foundry-agent-evaluation/deploy/experiment.py:254-371; no SAS retained.

functions.signature: readback_dataset(project, *, name: str, version: str, expected: bytes) -> {id, sha256, bytes, remote_bytes_verified: True, data_uri}
functions.behavior: get + get_credentials + blob properties/size + byte compare; refuses mismatch.

Exactly one: {type:file_content, content:[{item}]} or {type:file_id, id: dataset['id']}. agent_run_request delegates to it (evals.py:276-288 already has the branch; widen file_id to accept the record).

functions.signature: optimization_job(..., train: rows | DatasetRef, validation: rows | DatasetRef, ...)
functions.behavior: Keep inline_dataset for rows; reference_dataset for refs. Additive: existing train_items/validation_items keywords unchanged.

proposed_foundry_ops_api.manifest_binding: Record {split: {name, version, id, sha256}} beside dataset/manifest.json sha pins; derive projected bytes from the git-tracked JSONL so the registered sha is reproducible from source.

needs_live_write_to_prove: Register projected train/validation/verification JSONL (3 dataset versions; pending_upload + blob + create_or_update + get_credentials readback).
One eval run with file_id=<verification dataset id> against the accepted hosted version; compare row count/membership with the inline run.

One optimization job with train/validation {type:reference}; confirm acceptance, no opt-inline-* auto dataset created, candidates evaluated on the referenced rows; cost = same rows x candidates as inline.
Negative: reference with unknown version -> expected refusal (4xx), no job created.
Optional: JSONL with extra fields (unprojected) to learn tolerance; only if projection ownership is contested.
Teardown: datasets.delete for registered versions plus inventory of auto-created ones.
unknowns: Service row/byte limits for inline and dataset inputs.
Whether eval file_id accepts name/version instead of azureai:// id.
Whether optimization reference tolerates extra row fields.
Exact origin of each eval-data-* dataset (per-run correlation not done).
